objective:
Create a NEW, separate 'tag corpus' test set in core-testing for the subject+action tagging redesign. Background: today each capture is matched to one activity from a catalog; the redesign describes every entry with a SUBJECT tag (what it was done to: furnace, hot tub, lawn mower) and an ACTION tag (what was done: change filter, add gas, mow), plus an optional DURATION. An AI extracts subject/action/time words/duration/state as the user's own words (no catalog shown to it); deterministic program logic then resolves those words against existing subject and action tags (exact name -> alias -> close match) and a policy decides: AUTO_SAVE (silently logged), CONFIRM (quick 'did you mean X?' card; nothing saved silently), or NEEDS_REVIEW (nothing logged). This task only builds the TEST DATA, its Kotlin model/loader and its structural tests -- no resolver, no recorder, no scorer (later tasks).

DECISIONS ALREADY MADE (follow them):
(1) Separate file core-testing/src/main/resources/semantic-corpus/tag-corpus.json, LF line endings, UTF-8. Do NOT modify corpus.json (byte-exact SHA-256 is pinned by existing recordings; changing it would make them stale).
(2) Kotlin model in a new file TagCorpusModel.kt and loader TagCorpus.kt in package com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.testing.corpus (core-testing/src/main/kotlin/...). Mirror the style of CorpusModel.kt / SemanticCorpus.kt exactly: kotlinx.serialization, Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = false; explicitNulls = true }, every field without a default is REQUIRED including nullable ones, KDoc on every type/field, sha256 of the exact resource bytes, RESOURCE_PATH = "/semantic-corpus/tag-corpus.json", load()/parse(bytes), case(id). Reuse existing enums ActivityState, TimePrecision and CorpusCategory where they fit; add new enums as needed.
(3) Document shape: { schemaVersion: 1, description, catalogs: Map<String, TagCatalogFixture>, cases: List<TagCorpusCase> }.
  TagCatalogFixture = { description?, subjects: List<FixtureTag>, actions: List<FixtureTag>, pairs: List<FixturePair> } where FixtureTag = { id, displayName, aliases } and FixturePair = { subjectId, actionId, displayName } (a known subject+action combination, i.e. today's 'activity'; used later for inferring a missing subject and for lookup).
  TagCorpusCase = { id, group, category, catalog, rawText, capturedAt, zoneId, expected, note?, knownResolverGap?, sourceCaseId? }. `group` is a new enum TagCaseGroup { PORTED, REAL_ENTRY, SIBLING, EMPTY_START }. `sourceCaseId` is the corpus.json id for PORTED cases (required non-null there, null otherwise). `category` reuses CorpusCategory.
  expected = { subject: ExpectedTag, action: ExpectedTag, allowedStates: List<ActivityState?>, temporalExpression: String?, allowedTemporalExpressions: List<String?>, resolvedLocalDate: String?, precision: TimePrecision?, durationExpression: String?, allowedDurationExpressions: List<String?>, durationMinutes: Int?, outcome: TagOutcome, allowedOutcomes: List<TagOutcome> } with new enum TagOutcome { AUTO_SAVE, CONFIRM, NEEDS_REVIEW }.
  ExpectedTag = { existingId: String?, allowedExistingIds: List<String>, newName: String?, allowedNewNames: List<String>, mayBeEmpty: Boolean, mustNotMatch: List<String> }. Exactly one of existingId/newName is set, except both may be null only when mayBeEmpty is true or the outcome is NEEDS_REVIEW. existingId set = must resolve to that existing tag (creating a new one would be a duplicate). newName set = nothing suitable exists; a new tag with that name (or an allowed name, compared case-insensitively after trimming) is correct. mustNotMatch = existing tag ids that must never be chosen (use this to pin the WRONG tags the real entries were filed under).
  Add convenience getters like ExpectedInterpretation has (acceptableOutcomes, acceptableTemporalExpressions, expectedLocalDate, etc.).
(4) All cases use capturedAt "2026-09-15T20:00:00-04:00" and zoneId "America/Detroit" (same as corpus.json), so time words resolve identically.

CATALOG FIXTURES (ids are fixed, kebab-case, prefixed subj-/act-):
- `empty`: no subjects, actions or pairs.
- `household`: the tag form of corpus.json's household catalog. Subjects: lawn, furnace, gutters, dryer vent, leaves, car, fridge, garden, trash. Actions: mow, edge, replace filter, clean, blow, wax, replace water filter, water, take out. Pairs: lawn+mow 'Mow lawn', lawn+edge 'Edge lawn', furnace+replace filter 'Replace furnace filter', gutters+clean 'Clean gutters', dryer vent+clean 'Clean dryer vent', leaves+blow 'Blow leaves', car+wax 'Wax car', fridge+replace water filter 'Replace fridge water filter', garden+water 'Water garden', trash+take out 'Take out trash'. Carry over corpus.json's aliases in tag form only where they are genuine tag aliases (e.g. action replace water filter alias 'change water filter'; action blow alias 'leaf blowing' is fine on the action); do not invent extra aliases that would make synonym cases trivially easy.
- `household-no-edge`: household without action edge and without pair Edge lawn.
- `owner-2026-10-01`: the tag form of the owner's real catalog when the bad entries were recorded (Mow lawn, Trim hedges, Dishes, Hot tub, Walk dogs, Furnace maintenance, Reboot WiFi, Weed garden). Subjects: lawn, hedges, dishes, hot tub, dogs, furnace, WiFi (displayName exactly 'WiFi'), garden. Actions: mow, trim, wash, clean, walk, change filter, reboot, weed. Pairs: lawn+mow, hedges+trim, dishes+wash, hot tub+clean, dogs+walk, furnace+change filter, WiFi+reboot, garden+weed. No aliases.

CASES (target ~72; integrity test pins the exact counts you end up with):
A) PORTED (48): one case for EVERY case in corpus.json, same id as the source with prefix 'p-' (e.g. p-mow-i-cut-the-grass), sourceCaseId = source id, same rawText/capturedAt/zoneId/category, catalog = same fixture name (household/household-no-edge/empty), and identical allowedStates/temporalExpression/allowedTemporalExpressions/resolvedLocalDate/precision as the source. durationExpression/durationMinutes null (none of them state a duration). Subject/action expectations are the product-correct TAG reading: e.g. 'I cut the grass.' -> subject existing subj-lawn, action existing act-mow (the user's words differ from the tag names; deterministic matching may not catch it, which is what TG1.4 will measure -- the expectation stays product-correct). Where the user's words differ from the existing tag (grass/lawn, HVAC/furnace, air filter, 'did the gutters'), outcome AUTO_SAVE with allowedOutcomes [CONFIRM] (asking is acceptable, silently creating a duplicate tag is not). Where the sentence omits the subject but the action implies it via the fixture's only pair ('Finished mowing.', 'Just mowed.', 'Finished edging.'), subject existingId = the paired subject with mayBeEmpty true. Source NEW_ACTIVITY cases become new-tag expectations for whichever tag is new (e.g. 'Raked the leaves.' -> subject existing subj-leaves, action new 'rake'; 'Washed the car.' -> subject existing subj-car, action new 'wash', mustNotMatch [act-wax]; empty-catalog cases -> both new). Source NEAR_NEIGHBOUR mustNotMatch ids become the corresponding tag ids (e.g. edging must not match act-mow). Source AMBIGUITY cases -> outcome NEEDS_REVIEW, allowedOutcomes [CONFIRM], tags may be null with mayBeEmpty true. Source AUTO_ACCEPT -> AUTO_SAVE. Keep the source note text where useful and add a short note wherever the tag reading is non-obvious.
B) REAL_ENTRY (12), catalog owner-2026-10-01, rawText EXACTLY as below (these are real watch transcriptions, speech errors included -- do not correct them):
  1 'I just changed the furnace filter' -> furnace(existing) / change filter(existing); time 'just'.
  2 'I just changed the hot tub filter' -> hot tub(existing) / change filter(existing); mustNotMatch subject subj-furnace; time 'just'.
  3 'Yesterday I changed the oil in the tractor' -> tractor(new) / change oil(new); subject mustNotMatch subj-hot-tub; action mustNotMatch act-change-filter; time 'Yesterday' (allowed 'yesterday').
  4 'It just went and got gas for the lawn mower' -> lawn mower(new, NOT lawn: subject mustNotMatch subj-lawn) / get gas(new, allowed names 'add gas','buy gas'; mustNotMatch act-mow); time 'just'; outcome AUTO_SAVE allowed [CONFIRM] (lawn vs lawn mower is close).
  5 'I weeded the garden for half an hour' -> garden / weed (both existing); durationExpression 'for half an hour' (allowed 'half an hour'), durationMinutes 30; temporalExpression null (the duration is NOT a time) -- follow how corpus.json represents a capture with no time words; mustNotMatch subj-lawn/act-mow.
  6 'Yesterday I replaced the headlight on James Durango' -> new subject 'Durango' (allowed 'Dodge Durango'; mustNotMatch subj-lawn) / new action 'replace headlight' (mustNotMatch act-mow); time 'Yesterday'; outcome AUTO_SAVE allowed [CONFIRM]; note the speech error.
  7 'I just walked the dogs for about 30 minutes' -> dogs / walk (existing); time 'just'; durationExpression 'for about 30 minutes' (allowed 'about 30 minutes'), durationMinutes 30; mustNotMatch subj-lawn/act-mow.
  8 'Add to reboot the Wi-Fi' -> subj-wifi existing (must merge Wi-Fi with WiFi) / act-reboot existing; no time words; note: speech error for 'Had to'.
  9 'I just cleaned the hot tub' -> hot tub / clean (existing); mustNotMatch subj-dishes, act-wash; time 'just'.
  10 'Spent 40 minutes mowing the lawn' -> lawn / mow (existing); durationExpression '40 minutes' (allowed 'Spent 40 minutes'), durationMinutes 40; no time words.
  11 'I just put all the dishes away' -> dishes(existing) / put away(new; mustNotMatch act-wash); time 'just'.
  12 'Add sanitizer to the hot tub' -> hot tub(existing; mustNotMatch subj-dishes, subj-lawn) / add sanitizer(new); no time words.
  Categories: pick the closest existing CorpusCategory (SYNONYM for existing/existing, NEW_ACTIVITY where a tag is new, NEAR_NEIGHBOUR where a tempting wrong tag exists -- use your judgment and say so in `note`). Ids prefixed 'real-'.
C) SIBLING (8), catalog owner-2026-10-01, ids prefixed 'sib-': 'Drained the hot tub' (hot tub / new drain); 'Changed the filter in the hot tub' (hot tub / change filter, both existing, mustNotMatch subj-furnace); 'Changed the oil in the lawn mower' (new lawn mower, mustNotMatch subj-lawn / new change oil, mustNotMatch act-change-filter; allowed [CONFIRM]); 'Washed the dogs' (dogs / wash, both existing, though never paired); 'Cleaned the furnace' (furnace / clean, both existing, mustNotMatch subj-hot-tub); 'Rebooted the router' (new router, mustNotMatch subj-wifi, allowed [CONFIRM] / reboot existing); 'Weeded the flower bed' (new flower bed, mustNotMatch subj-garden, allowed [CONFIRM] / weed existing); 'Added chlorine to the hot tub' (hot tub existing / new add chlorine). No time words in any.
D) EMPTY_START (4), catalog empty, ids prefixed 'empty-': rawTexts identical to real entries 1, 6, 7, 8. All tags new (e.g. 'Wi-Fi' allowed ['WiFi','wifi']); same time/duration expectations as the real entries; outcome AUTO_SAVE.

TESTS (core-testing/src/test/kotlin/com/mcfrenchpants/activityledger/core/testing/corpus/):
- TagCorpusIntegrityTest: loads via TagCorpus.load(); unique kebab-case ids; parseable capture context; every catalog reference exists; every existingId/allowedExistingIds/mustNotMatch id exists in that case's fixture under the right kind (subject ids among subjects, action ids among actions); fixture tag ids unique per fixture and pair ids resolve; ExpectedTag consistency rules from (3) (existingId xor newName unless mayBeEmpty/NEEDS_REVIEW; existingId never in mustNotMatch or allowedExistingIds; newName set => existingId null; empty catalog => no existingId); allowedOutcomes never repeats outcome; durationMinutes > 0 exactly when durationExpression set; resolvedLocalDate/precision set exactly when temporalExpression set; every corpus.json case has exactly one PORTED case with matching sourceCaseId, rawText, capturedAt, zoneId, category, allowedStates and temporal fields (load SemanticCorpus to compare); sourceCaseId non-null iff group PORTED; the 12 REAL_ENTRY rawTexts equal the exact strings above; pinned counts per group and per outcome.
